name: Goldbach

phase_0.boundary_condition: The set of even integers greater than two

VINIT.justification: The state before an even integer is selected for decomposition.

TANCH.justification: The terminal constraint defining the valid input space for the conjecture.

AFWD.justification: The forward selection of the first valid prime pair (p, q).

AREV.justification: The reverse search for an integer lacking a prime decomposition.

CLINK.justification: The sequential concatenation of verified integers into a continuous record.

IMSCRIB.justification: The self-recognition of the integer as a sum of its parts.

FSPLIT.justification: The bifurcation of an integer into its full set of prime-pair representations.

FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of the original integer from any selected prime pair.

EVALT.justification: The affirmative state where at least one prime pair is found.

EVALF.justification: The negative state indicating a potential counterexample.

ENGAGR.justification: The paradice state where multiple valid decompositions coexist without preference.

IFIX.justification: The irreversible fixation of a verified integer into the global history.

phase_3.false_description: no prime pair exists for the given integer
phase_3.both_description: multiple distinct prime pair decompositions exist

steps.domain_action: initialize the word tape to the void state
impose the boundary condition that n is an even integer greater than two
bifurcate the integer n into the set of all possible prime pairs p and q
anchor the T-arm by confirming the existence of at least one pair
select the lexicographically first prime pair from the T-arm
reconstitute the integer n from the selected prime pair to verify integrity
recognize the identity of n through the sum of the selected primes
anchor the F-arm to monitor for the absence of prime pairs
initiate a reverse trace if the F-arm is activated to record the failure
close the F-arm to maintain Frobenius symmetry
append the verified integer to the sequential chain of evidence
engage the status register to hold the state of multiple decompositions
permanently record the verification of n in the append-only ledger
close the protocol by confirming the self-consistency of the final state

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The primality testing and subtraction logic
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Tuple passing between decomposition and reconstruction functions
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The global verified dictionary and history list
phase_5.alfs_store: The Oliveira e Silva computational verification records

phase_6.cycle_cost: CPU cycles for primality verification and memory for the evidence chain
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A permanently fixed record of n as a sum of primes
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The information content of n is exactly preserved in its prime components.
